resources.string: Start automatically when the phone boots
Waiting for the deck to start…
Installing/updating the deck inside Ubuntu (the first run can take several minutes)…
127.0.0.1 = this phone only · 0.0.0.0 = whole network (requires a password)
A password is required to expose the deck on the network
Adds system info, terminal self-tests and debug-level server logs to the log. Applies after Stop → Start.
Off by default. Lets the AI agents in the deck read the battery and device info and send notifications to this phone. Applies after Stop → Start.

AI agents running in the deck will be able to read information from this phone (battery, device) and show notifications on it. More abilities may come later. An agent can be tricked by text in a web page, file or message (prompt injection) into using what it can reach. Turn this on only if you understand that and want it.
You can turn this off here at any time. Agents only get what this switch allows, and each request is written to the log. Enable phone access?
Notifications are off for this app. Turn them on in the page that opens.
Shared folder: agents see only the folder “CLI Deck” of your phone, at /root/phone in the terminal. All storage: the whole internal storage, at /sdcard. Applies after Stop → Start.

Agents will be able to read and change everything in the “CLI Deck” folder of your phone (at /root/phone), and nothing else. Put there only what you are happy for them to see. Android will ask for storage permission. Continue?

Agents will be able to read, change and delete ANY file in your phone storage: photos, documents, downloads, other apps’ files. A tricked agent could leak or destroy them. Prefer “Shared folder only”. Android will ask for storage permission. Continue with all storage?
Permission not granted: that feature stays off.
Turn on “Allow access to all files” for this app on the page that opens.
An agent wants to connect this phone to the Wi-Fi network “%1$s”.
An agent wants to turn Wi-Fi on.
An agent wants to turn Wi-Fi off.
This lets agents do something harmless but noticeable on your phone. Android may ask for a permission.

This reaches personal information or the world around you (location, network, camera, microphone). Agents can be tricked by text in web pages or files (prompt injection) into using it, and what they read goes to the AI provider. Enable only if you accept that.

This reaches your private data or lets agents act in your name or spend money (contacts, messages, calls, calendar). A tricked agent could leak or misuse it. Every use waits for your tap on Allow, but read each request carefully. Enable only if you really need it.
Turn on “Modify system settings” for this app on the page that opens.
Turn on “Share to the deck” in the CLI Deck settings first.
Read and write the phone’s clipboard (reading only works while CLI Deck is on screen).
Turn the flashlight on or off.
Read and set the screen brightness (needs “Modify system settings”).
Read text aloud on the phone.
Adds “Send to CLI Deck” to Android’s share sheet; shared items go to /root/inbox.
See the current and nearby networks; changes need your tap on Allow. Asks for the location permission.
Take photos (each needs your tap on Allow); saved to /root/inbox.
Record short audio clips (each needs your tap on Allow); saved to /root/inbox.
See and switch Bluetooth (switching needs your tap on Allow).
Search your contacts (each search needs your tap on Allow).
Send and read text messages (each use needs your tap on Allow).
Place calls and read the call log (each use needs your tap on Allow).
Read and add events (each use needs your tap on Allow).
